summary.text: A 60-year-old right-handed man had a cryptogenetic ischaemic stroke from a left MCA occlusion 14 months before his first visit. He presented with severe non-fluent aphasia with retained comprehension, dyslexia, dysgraphia, right upper limb spastic paralysis and right lower limb paresis, plus post-stroke depression. Physiotherapy and speech therapy had just been finished with minimal results.

Brain MR before HBOT showed an established ischaemic lesion in the deep and superficial left MCA territory with a wide malacic area, capsulo-lenticular, insular and corona radiata involvement, frontal operculum and fronto-lateral cortex malacia and left ventricular ex-vacuum enlargement. Task fMRI was obtained a few days before and after 40 HBOT sessions.

He completed 40 HBOT sessions with restarted speech therapy and physiotherapy, without complications. After HBOT aphasia improved noticeably, he regained some social life with better mood, and right lower limb paresis improved, while right hand paralysis did not improve apart from decreased spasticity. fMRI showed a new right frontal opercular activation and lesions unchanged on MR.

summary.text: A 68-year-old right-handed man presented with a chronic multifocal encephalopathy from recurrent cerebral ischaemic strokes that began 5 years earlier. Examination showed moderate signs of dysarthria, an unsteady wide-base gait and dysphagia. He did not undergo physiotherapy or speech therapy.

Brain MR before HBOT showed many bilateral gliotic areas, prevalent on the right, in the subcortical and para-ventricular deep white matter, extending to the basal ganglia and the right pons, consistent with chronic small vessels disease. fMRI was obtained a few days before and after 40 HBOT sessions.

He completed 40 HBOT sessions without complications. After HBOT he showed marked improvement in language fluency, reading aloud a written text without a hitch, and ataxia and dysphagia improved. fMRI showed more extended and more significant language-task activations, a new right-sided area, and unchanged lesion morphology on MR.

Examination showed mild signs of dysarthria, left upper limb paralysis, left lower limb paresis and right limb incoordination. He refused speech therapy and rehabilitation but decided to practice swimming.

Brain MR before HBOT showed a very wide right fronto-parieto-temporal malacic area with right lateral ventricle ex-vacuo enlargement, a bulky arachnoid cyst from the temporal pole to the anterior Sylvian region and a smaller parietal cyst. fMRI was obtained a few days before and after 40 HBOT sessions.

He completed 40 HBOT sessions without complications. After HBOT his speech fluency dramatically improved, left lower limb paresis and right limb coordination improved, but he remained unable to flex and extend the left foot rhythmically and the left upper limb paralysis did not change. fMRI showed bilateral temporal language areas after HBOT and unchanged lesion morphology.

summary.text: A 34-year-old right-handed man had a haemorrhagic transformation of an ischaemic stroke in the left MCA territory 17 months earlier. Examination showed global non-fluent aphasia with some reading comprehension deficits, complete spastic hemiplegia of the right upper limb with spastic hypertonia, partial paresis of the right inferior limb with walking aids, and right hemilateral hypoaesthesia, without speech therapy or rehabilitation.

Brain MR before HBOT showed a gliotic-malacic area in the left capsulo-lenticular nucleus partially involving the insula, extending to the left caudate nucleus and ipsilateral corona radiata, with moderate dilatation of the left lateral ventricle. fMRI was obtained a few days before and after 40 HBOT sessions.

He completed 40 HBOT sessions without complications. After HBOT he showed good improvement in speaking, understanding and walking, but not in his upper limb paralysis. fMRI showed more extended language activations with new right-sided and second fronto-opercular areas, no left hand motor area activation on imagined right hand movement, and unchanged lesion morphology.
